THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Though this matter is listed for admission, with consent of learned counsel for parties, it is taken-up for final disposal.

2. Challenging common judgment and award dated 29.09.2016, passed by Principal Motor Accident Claims Tribunal and Principal District and Sessions Judge, Bidar, (for short, 'tribunal') in MVC no.599/2014, this appeal is filed.

entities.text: Principal District and Sessions Judge, Bidar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Shri Santosh Biradar, learned counsel for appellant submitted that this appeal was filed by claimant for enhancement of compensation.

It was submitted that in claim petition, tribunal had on contest held that claimant - Santosh sustained grievous injuries in accident NC: 2023:KHC-K:6506 caused due to rash and negligent driving of insured vehicle (motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-38/K-8133) on 06.06.2014, vehicle was insured with respondent no.2 - insurer, valid as on date of accident and therefore it was liable to pay compensation.
It was submitted that since insurer had not preferred appeal against said award, findings of tribunal had attained finality.

4. Insofar as appeal for enhancement, it was submitted that as on date of accident claimant was 25 years of age, working as Manager in Greenland Bar and Restaurant and earning `10,000/- per month sustained fracture of frontal bone and Sub-dural Haematoma, Cerebral edema requiring craniotomy twice, but resulting in claimant suffering from 'Organic brain syndrome'.
It was submitted that said disability was assessed by PW.2 to an extent of 50%.

However, tribunal considered meager monthly income of `6,000/-, disability at 20% and awarded inadequate Santosh S/O Rajesh vs Girishkumar S/O Satyanarayan And Anr on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157500840/
2 compensation.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:6506 5.

entities.text: Santosh S/O Rajesh vs Girishkumar S/O Satyanarayan And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was submitted that even compensation awarded towards pain and suffering and other incidental expenses were on lower side, while no compensation was awarded towards loss of amenities, loss of income during laid-up period, loss of marriage prospects and towards future medical expenses.
On above grounds, learned counsel sought for allowing appeal.
6. On other hand, Smt.Shashikala Jahagirdar, learned counsel for respondent no.2-insurer sought to support award and oppose enhancement.
It was submitted that no evidence was led to establish that claimant was working as Manager in hotel.
There was no basis for claiming future medical expenses or for loss of marriage prospects.

It was submitted that based on available material, tribunal had assessed compensation under various heads as required and therefore no interference was called for.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:6506 7.
Heard.
Perused impugned judgment and award and record.

8. From above submission, since only claimant is in appeal for enhancement of compensation, point that arises for consideration is :
"Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for ?"
9.

Though claimant is stated that he was 25 years of age, working as Manager and earning `10,000/-
per month, same is not substantiated with specific evidence.
In absence, tribunal assessed it notionally.
But, notional income for year 2014 adopted for settlement of cases before Lok-Adalat is `7,500/-.
Therefore, same has to be considered.

10. Insofar as disability, claimant relied on wound certificate, discharge summary, medical reports,
bills, prescriptions, ECG, x-ray films and disability certificate NC: 2023:KHC-K:6506 marked as Ex.P.5 to P.14 respectively.
In support of said materials, he also examined Dr.S.S.Bhairwadgi as PW.2.
In Ex.P.14, PW.2 has assessed disability to extent of 50% by observing that claimant was suffering from 'Organic brain syndrome'.
He has reiterated same in his deposition.
While passing impugned award, tribunal observed that there was no evidence led to establish that claimant was in vegetative state and unable to perform his day to day activities etc.
But, assuming possibility of disability affecting earning capacity to some extent, it considered functional disability at 20%.

On perusal of cross- examination of PW.1-father of claimant and PW.2 - Doctor by insurer, it is seen that there are no suggestions about possibility of claimant carrying on his occupation as before or about disability not causing loss of earning capacity.

Under such circumstances, considering age,
occupation and nature of disability, it would be appropriate to enhance physical disability to 30%.

Further, Hon'ble NC: 2023:KHC-K:6506 Supreme Court in case of Erudaya Priya v/s State Express Transport Corporation Limited1, has held that even in injury cases, claimant would be entitled for Santosh S/O Rajesh vs Girishkumar S/O Satyanarayan And Anr on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157500840/
3 addition of future prospects.

sentences.text:
Considering claimant was below 40 years of age and self-employed,
future prospects at 40% has to be added.
11.
By referring to age mentioned in disability certificate, tribunal held claimant was 26 years of age.
But, Ex.P.5 - wound certificate and other medical records show his age as 25 years.

Admittedly,
disability certificate is issued much after date of accident.

Therefore, future loss of income would be -
`7,500 + 40% X 30% X 12 X 18 = `6,80,400/-.
12.
Claimant sustained fracture of frontal bone and underwent craniotomy twice and would have underwent severe pain and sufferings.
Therefore grant of only `30,000/- would be inadequate and it would be AIR 2020 SC 4284 NC: 2023:KHC-K:6506 appropriate to enhance it to `75,000/-.
Tribunal has awarded `4,53,500/- towards medical expenses against bills produced in complete reimbursement.
Hence, there is no scope for enhancement.

For inpatient treatment of 45 days,
tribunal has awarded only `10,000/- towards miscellaneous and other incidental expenses, which would be inadequate.
Considering facts and circumstances, it would be appropriate to enhance it to `25,000/-.
13. Tribunal has not awarded compensation towards loss of amenities.
Taking note of injuries/disability sustained, it would be appropriate to award sum of `50,000/- towards loss of amenities.
Normally fractures take about three months to heal.
Since claimant has taken inpatient treatment for 45 days, it would be appropriate to consider four months as period of lay-off.
At `7,500/- per month, it would be `30,000/- which is awarded.
14. Insofar as future medical expenses, neither in evidence of claimant nor that of Doctor, there is any NC: 2023:KHC-K:6506 reference to need or necessity of future treatment.
Therefore, there cannot be award towards future medical expenses.
Even insofar as loss of marriage prospects, no evidential basis is placed.
Therefore, compensation towards same can be assessed notionally.
Considering age of claimant at 25 years, it would be appropriate to award sum of `25,000/- towards loss of marriage prospects.
15. Thus, total compensation would be `13,38,900/-.
Point no.2 is answered partly in affirmative.

Consequently, following:
ORDER Appeal is allowed in part with costs.
Claimant is held entitled for total compensation of `13,38,900/- with interest at 6% p.a. from date of claim petition till deposit.
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6506 Respondent no.2-insurer to deposit enhanced compensation within six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
